name: CampusVote
tagline: Verifiable, anonymous e-voting for student elections
problem: Paper ballots: hours of manual counting, disputed recounts
Google Forms: admins see who voted what and can edit rows
Shared form links and proxy logins allow double voting
Losing candidates have no way to check the result

stats.label: ways for a voter to check a Google Forms tally
to hand-count a few thousand paper ballots (approx.)
can silently edit a spreadsheet of votes

solution: Chaum blind signatures: eligible, yet unlinkable to the voter
SHA-256 commitments hide choices until voting closes
Hash-chained public bulletin board with signed checkpoints
Receipts + full recount by anyone, even in the browser

features.title: Phone voting
features.desc: Mobile-first ballot over campus Wi-Fi, large buttons, no app

features.title: Blind-signed tokens
features.desc: Authority signs a token it never sees; one per register number

features.title: Public bulletin board
features.desc: Hash chain + RSA-signed checkpoints, download and verify anywhere

features.title: Voter receipts
features.desc: Check on your own phone that your ballot was counted as cast

features.title: Attack lab
features.desc: 12 live attacks: double vote, forgery, replay, tampering, stuffing

features.title: Explained audit
features.desc: 10-step verification report with the reason each check matters

architecture: Phone/browser (vanilla JS) -> SHA-256, RSA blinding, sealing, audit
app.py ThreadingHTTPServer -> JSON API, no IPs logged on cast
election.py -> roster, OTP login, issuance, mix pool, phases, tally
blind.py + rsa.py + numtheory.py -> Miller-Rabin, RSA-FDH, Chaum
board.py + audit.py -> hash chain, checkpoints, universal recount
data/board.json -> the only file an auditor needs
algorithms: RSA-FDH + CRT - signatures with Bellcore fault check
Chaum blind signatures - eligibility without identity
SHA-256 hash commitments - hiding and binding ballots
RSA-KEM + SHA-256 CTR + HMAC - sealed openings for the trustee
Hash chain + signed checkpoints - tamper-evident board
tech: Python 3 stdlib only (hashlib, hmac, secrets, http.server)
Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with BigInt crypto, inline SVG charts
Fully offline: one laptop + campus Wi-Fi
innovation: Admin can run the election but cannot see, link or alter votes
Browser re-verifies the whole board: no trust in our server
Perfect unlinkability shown live: every pairing is consistent
Honest threat model, incl. coercion and stuffing limits

results.label: blind signature per voter, 2048-bit, pure Python

demo_flow: Phone: demo voter signs in, gets a blind-signed token
Choose candidates, cast anonymously, get a receipt
Attack lab: double vote, forgery, replay all rejected
Edit board.json: chain breaks at the exact entry; restore
Close voting: trustee opens ballots, signed result posted
Phone re-checks receipt: counted exactly as cast
impact: Results in minutes, not an evening of counting
Disputes settled by recounting a public file
Students can vote from hostels and labs on their phones
No paper ballots to print for every election
business: Free for student clubs on one laptop
Annual college licence: council, hostel, club and alumni polls
Paid audit/observer support for university-wide elections
Extend to RWAs, cooperatives and union ballots
future: Split trustee and signing keys across 3 faculty (threshold RSA)
Real mix-net / separate relay so the server never sees ballot IPs
Homomorphic ElGamal tally with zero-knowledge ballot proofs
